title: Uttarakhand Tunnel Collapse Death Toll Rises to Eight as Rescue Teams Search for Two Missing Workers
excerpt: A flooded tunnel in Chamoli district has claimed eight lives, with rescue operations continuing for two workers still unaccounted for. Survivors say warnings about leaks and debris went unheeded.
body:
• Eight workers have died in a tunnel collapse in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district, with search operations continuing for two who remain missing.
  • Surviving workers said they had reported leaks and falling debris inside the tunnel before the collapse but received no response from supervisors.
  • The disaster adds to Uttarakhand's grim record of infrastructure accidents, including the 2023 Silkyara tunnel collapse that trapped 41 workers for 17 days and a Sikkim tunnel blast that killed 25 in July 2026.
  • The incident has reignited calls for stricter safety oversight of tunnel construction in the geologically fragile Himalayan region.

The death toll from a tunnel collapse in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district has risen to eight, with rescue teams continuing to search for two workers still trapped inside the flooded structure, according to NDTV and The Hindu.

What Happened

The tunnel, part of ongoing infrastructure construction in the mountainous district, collapsed after heavy monsoon rainfall caused flooding inside the structure. Ten workers were inside at the time of the collapse. Eight bodies have been recovered so far, while search operations continue for the remaining two, hampered by waterlogging and debris.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2088606469256069513

The National Disaster Response Force and State Disaster Response Force teams have been deployed to the site, working alongside local authorities. Heavy rains across the region have complicated rescue efforts, with officials warning of continued landslide risk in the area.

Workers Say Warnings Were Ignored

In accounts reported by NDTV, surviving workers from the project said they had flagged leaks and falling debris inside the tunnel before the collapse. They said their warnings were not acted upon by supervisors or project management, raising serious questions about safety protocols at the construction site.

The accounts echo a pattern that has emerged across India's ambitious infrastructure push in the Himalayas, where rapid construction timelines often collide with fragile geology and extreme weather conditions.

Uttarakhand's Recurring Infrastructure Tragedies

The Chamoli tunnel collapse is the latest in a series of deadly infrastructure accidents in India's mountainous northern states. In July 2026, a methane gas explosion inside a hydropower tunnel in neighbouring Sikkim killed all 25 workers trapped inside. The 2023 Silkyara tunnel collapse in Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi district trapped 41 workers for 17 days before they were rescued through manual mining methods, triggering a national conversation about tunnel safety.

Uttarakhand's Chamoli district has been particularly prone to disasters. In February 2021, a glacial flood killed nearly 200 people and destroyed two hydropower projects in the same district. Scientists have warned that climate change is increasing the intensity of extreme weather events in the Himalayas, while accelerating construction compounds the risk.

The Broader Safety Debate

India's infrastructure expansion in the Himalayas — including the Char Dham highway project connecting major Hindu pilgrimage sites — has faced persistent criticism from environmental scientists and safety experts. Critics argue that construction in the young, geologically unstable mountain range requires more rigorous safety standards and environmental impact assessments than current protocols demand.

The incident occurred on the eve of India's 80th Independence Day, casting a shadow over national celebrations. Rescue operations at the Chamoli site are expected to continue as weather permits.
